#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --account=normal
#   --job-name=elp
#   --output=logs/output-ep-pr-%j.log
#   --error=logs/output-ep-pr-%j.err
#   --time=1-00:00:00
#   --mem=50gb
#   -p gpu
#   -N 2
#   -n 2
#   --exclude=pgpu01

#flux: --job-name=elp
#flux: -N 2
#flux: -n 2
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=50gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p gpu (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on non-GPU nodes or have different limits/priority (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm option: --account=normal
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted Slurm option: --exclude=pgpu01
# Flux node exclusion is site/config dependent; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on undesired nodes, potentially affecting performance or reliability.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

ulimit -c 256
nvidia-smi

source activate lipinggpu

# If the job should run once (not 2-way parallel), requesting -n 2 may waste resources.
# Preserve the Slurm request of 2 tasks by launching under Flux.
flux run -n 2 -c 1 stdbuf -o0 python -u run-exp.py kegg_20_maccs -m ep -e pr --random_seed 1997

reasons: The original Slurm job requested 50GB of memory (`--mem=50gb`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
The original Slurm job targeted the GPU partition (`-p gpu`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition constraint; the allocation may land on non-GPU nodes or be rejected by policy.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
#
#SBATCH --account=normal
#
#SBATCH --job-name=elp
#
## output files
#SBATCH --output=logs/output-ep-pr-%j.log
#SBATCH --error=logs/output-ep-pr-%j.err
#
# Estimated running time. 
# The job will be killed when it runs 15 min longer than this time.
#SBATCH --time=1-00:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=50gb
#
## Resources 
## -p gpu/batch  |job type
## -N            |number of nodes
## -n            |number of cpu 
#SBATCH -p gpu 
#SBATCH -N 2
#SBATCH -n 2
#SBATCH --exclude=pgpu01
ulimit -c 256
nvidia-smi
source activate lipinggpu
stdbuf -o0 python -u run-exp.py kegg_20_maccs -m ep -e pr --random_seed 1997
